title: What You Must Tell ATC
hook: Some silence is golden. This silence is a violation.

scenes.narration: Thirty seconds. Required reports. ATC isn't clingy — some things they legally have to hear.
Always: leaving an altitude. A missed approach. True airspeed off five percent or ten knots. Altitude changes V F R on top.
Also always: can't climb five hundred a minute, entering or leaving a hold, and anything broken. Confession is free — the ramp check isn't.
Off radar? Add position reports, and an E T A off by three minutes. Yes kid, we did that daily. Uphill. Both ways.
When in doubt, key up. Nobody ever failed a checkride for talking too politely.
A I M five dash three dash three. The full guest list.

quiz.question: Which of these must ALWAYS be reported to ATC, radar or not?
choices: Vacating a previously assigned altitude for a new one
quiz.explanation: Leaving an assigned altitude for a newly assigned one is on the always-report list. (AIM 5-3-3)

quiz.question: You must report a change in average true airspeed of:
quiz.explanation: A TAS change of 5% or 10 knots (whichever is greater) from what's filed must be reported.

quiz.question: A report required only when NOT in radar contact:
choices: Position over each compulsory reporting point
quiz.explanation: Compulsory position reports (and ETA changes >3 min) apply in a non-radar environment; the others are always required.
